This repository was build for the final project for MIDS 203 - Section 7
Team. The team includes - Kala Fejzo - Shola Able-Thomas - Emmanuel
Damas - Hope Tadsen

This project is the data exploration and modeling set of work based on a
data set with variables representing mental health scores across genres
and other variables. The data was collected through random respondents
to a Reddit post and therefore can be assumed to be IID though this may
seem a flimsy argument considering the lack of principles or rules
around who has access to or uses that website.

This project examines the relationship between daily music listening
habits and mental health outcomes. The research question asks: how do
hours of music listened to per day (X) influence an individual’s mental
health score (Y)? The null hypothesis (H₀) is that hours of music per
day do not impact mental health, while the alternative hypothesis (Hₐ)
is that increased music listening positively impacts mental health. This
question is relevant in the broader context of growing interest in
digital media’s influence on mental well-being, especially as streaming
platforms, such as Spotify and Apple Music, become increasingly more
popular in everyday life. The primary audience for this research
includes streaming platforms and their marketing teams who can benefit
from understanding how user engagement with music relates to mental
health. Insights from this analysis could inform platform design,
personalized recommendations, and targeted marketing strategies that
emphasize wellness benefits. This area has been explored in the past,
one of which discusses the impact music has on immunity. This was
written by Lavinia Rebecchini, PhD, and she argued that music is an
integral part of development and “can positively influence physiological
processes that enhance physical and mental wellbeing.” Given these
previous works we endeavor to better understand the relationship between
music and mental health indicators. The dataset (named MxMH) was
collected using an online google form survey, which was advertised
widely using physical pamphlets and on social media platforms such as
Reddit and Discord, between July 27th - November 11th, 2022. There were
no restrictions placed on age or location. The form utilized a
self-reported mental health scale which scored Depression, Anxiety,
Insomnia and OCD on a range from 0 (I do not experience this) to 10 (I
experience this regularly, or to an extreme). The study aims to evaluate
the relationship between the daily number of hours listened to music and
the combined mental health score. If a relationship truly exists, music
listening could be categorized into separate genres, mainly Classical,
Country, EDM, Folk, Gospel, Hip-Hop, Jazz, K-pop, Latin, Lofi, Metal,
Pop, R&B, Rap, Rock and Video game, with a secondary aim to further
assess the impact of each genre on individual mental health states.
